Cycling in the US from a Dutch perspective
Would actually love to get a bicycle but a good one is incredibly expensive unless I'm just looking in the wrong place?

No, you're not looking in the wrong place. I find that here in North America biking as the videos says is viewed as something for children or as a hobby rather than a legitimate form of transit - hence you have the "mountain bikes" that you can find at any walmart and are shit quality, the kind that kids use and then you have the "tour de France" racing style bikes for the adult hobbyists who are really into cycling which are both expensive and not really what a casual rider is looking for. The best bikes for casual commuting are the Dutch style "omafiets/opafiets" which are mainstream in Europe and must certainly be more affordable over there, but here in North America are usually imported (expensive), and despite having a surge in popularity recently are still not considered mainstream enough to bring in more of them to meet demand (thus keeping them expensive). My best guess (if you have the knowhow) would be to maybe make your own custom bike from parts, that way you can control the quality and customize it for what you use it most for, while still (likely) being cheaper that an entirely brand new high quality bike.
